- [x] **Formatting issues have been fixed** (run `pnpm prettier-fix`)
  - Code follows consistent formatting patterns, all Prettier checks pass
  
- [x] **I have reviewed this pull request** (self-review)
  - Verified minimal scope, surgical fix preserving existing behavior
  - Confirmed all edge cases handled with comprehensive test coverage



## Future Work

**Potential follow-up improvements (not in scope for this bug fix):**

1. **Performance optimization**: Cache content filtering results for large message arrays
2. **Enhanced testing**: Add performance benchmarks for message conversion with tools
3. **Error messaging**: Provide more descriptive errors when Claude validation fails
4. **Documentation**: Add examples to docs showing proper tool calling message flows

*Note: These are enhancements, not requirements for fixing the reported bug.*

title: chore(repo): make clean scripts cross-platform (replace rm -rf with del-cli)
body:
Fixes #8496

- Updated all package.json clean scripts: rm -rf → del-cli
- Added del-cli as dev dependency at workspace root
- No runtime code changes, dev-only cross-platform fix
- Verified on Windows: clean/build/test now work vs previous rm errors

## Background

On Windows, `rm` is not available by default, causing all clean/build/test commands to fail with `'rm' is not recognized as an internal or external command`. This completely blocks Windows contributors and CI runners from using the development toolchain.

The issue affects 40+ packages across the monorepo, all using `rm -rf` in their clean scripts. @gr2m recommended the `del-cli` approach in the issue comments.


## Summary

Replaced Unix-only `rm -rf` commands with cross-platform `del-cli` in all package.json clean scripts:

- **Before**: `"clean": "rm -rf dist *.tsbuildinfo"`
- **After**: `"clean": "del-cli dist *.tsbuildinfo"`

Added `del-cli` as a dev-only dependency at the workspace root. No runtime code changes, no published API changes.


## Manual Verification

**Before this PR (Windows PowerShell):**
```powershell
pnpm run clean
# Error: 'rm' is not recognized as an internal or external command
```

**After this PR (Windows PowerShell):**
```powershell
pnpm run clean    #  Works - cleans dist and .tsbuildinfo files
pnpm build        #  Works - builds successfully after clean
pnpm test         #  Works - 79/80 packages pass (RSC fails due to Playwright setup, unrelated)
```

**Cross-platform verification:**
- Unix/macOS behavior unchanged (del-cli works identically to rm -rf)
- All lint/type-check validations pass

Fixes Anthropic API error where tool_result wasn't immediately following tool_use.

title: feat(ai): extend addToolResult to support error results
body:
<!--
Welcome to contributing to AI SDK! We're excited to see your changes.

We suggest you read the following contributing guide we've created before submitting:

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

## Background

<!-- Why was this change necessary? -->

Currently the `addToolResult()` helper allows a user to update a pending tool call evaluated on the client. However, there is not currently a mechanism for being able to report a pending tool call as errored with a state of `output-error`.

We would like to be able to use this to report client side errors with failed tool calls as well as cancellations.

There doesn't appear to be a way to replicate the behavior of the `addToolResult` implementation using just the public API provided by `useChat`.

So as a workaround we currently have to use `addToolResult` and add an additional typed field on our tool output with `status: "success" | "error"` and consider failed tool calls "output" then adapt the rendering in our application. This differs to how we handle server side errors with tool calls which will use the `output-error` state.

```ts
const { messages, sendMessage, addToolResult } = useChat({
  transport: new DefaultChatTransport({
    api: '/api/chat',
  }),

  sendAutomaticallyWhen: lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls,

  // run client-side tools that are automatically executed:
  async onToolCall({ toolCall }) {
    // Check if it's a dynamic tool first for proper type narrowing
    if (toolCall.dynamic) {
      return;
    }

    if (toolCall.toolName === 'getWeatherInformation') {
      try {
        const weather = await getWeatherInformation(toolCall.input);

        // No await - avoids potential deadlocks
        addToolResult({
          tool: 'getWeatherInformation',
          toolCallId: toolCall.toolCallId,
          output: {
            status: "success",
            value: cities[Math.floor(Math.random() * cities.length)],
          }
        });
      } catch (err) {
        addToolResult({
          tool: 'getWeatherInformation',
          toolCallId: toolCall.toolCallId,
          output: {
            status: "error",
            value: "Failed to get weather information",
          }
        });
      }
    }
  },
});
```

Then in our UI code when handling the tool part:

```tsx
const status = useMemo((): React.ReactNode => {
  if (cancelled) {
    return <ErrorIcon />;
  }

  switch (state) {
    case "input-available":
    case "input-streaming":
      return (
        <Spinner />
      );
    case "output-available":
      // Duplicate error handling.
      if (output.type === "error") {
        return (
          <ErrorIcon />
        );
      }
      return (
        <SuccessIcon />
      );
    case "output-error":
      return (
        <ErrorIcon />
      );
    default:
      const exhaustive: never = state;
      throw new Error(`Unexpected state: ${exhaustive}`);
  }
}, [state, output, cancelled]);
```

## Summary

This commit extends the `addToolResult` method on the `AbstractChat` class to optionally take an `output-error` result. This allows clients to report both successful and failed tool calls using the same mechanism.

```ts
addToolResult({ tool, toolCallId, state: "output-error", errorText: "Failed" });
```

For backwards compatibility the existing method interface is still supported and will default to a state of `output-available`.

```ts
addToolResult({ tool, toolCallId, output: "Success!" });
```

So my earlier example becomes:

```ts
const { messages, sendMessage, addToolResult } = useChat({
  transport: new DefaultChatTransport({
    api: '/api/chat',
  }),

  sendAutomaticallyWhen: lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls,

  // run client-side tools that are automatically executed:
  async onToolCall({ toolCall }) {
    // Check if it's a dynamic tool first for proper type narrowing
    if (toolCall.dynamic) {
      return;
    }

    if (toolCall.toolName === 'getWeatherInformation') {
      try {
        const weather = await getWeatherInformation(toolCall.input);

        // No await - avoids potential deadlocks
        addToolResult({
          tool: 'getWeatherInformation',
          toolCallId: toolCall.toolCallId,
          output: cities[Math.floor(Math.random() * cities.length)],
        });
      } catch (err) {
        addToolResult({
          tool: 'getWeatherInformation',
          toolCallId: toolCall.toolCallId,
          state: "output-error",
          errorText: "Failed to get weather information",
        });
      }
    }
  },
});
```

Integration style tests have been added to the existing chat.test.ts suite to exercise the new behavior in the same fashion as the current implementation.

It also updates the `lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls` helper function to also consider tool parts with a state of `output-error` a completed tool call. This ensures consistent behavior for both types of result.

## Notes on implementation

I've extended `addToolResult` to keep the API footprint minimal but I would appreciate feedback on whether an additional method e.g. `addToolError({ tool, toolCallId, errorText })` would be a more appropriate solution. I'm happy to change the code if needed.

```ts
const { messages, sendMessage, addToolResult } = useChat({
  transport: new DefaultChatTransport({
    api: '/api/chat',
  }),

  sendAutomaticallyWhen: lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls,

  // run client-side tools that are automatically executed:
  async onToolCall({ toolCall }) {
    // Check if it's a dynamic tool first for proper type narrowing
    if (toolCall.dynamic) {
      return;
    }

    if (toolCall.toolName === 'getWeatherInformation') {
      try {
        const weather = await getWeatherInformation(toolCall.input);

        // No await - avoids potential deadlocks
        addToolResult({
          tool: 'getWeatherInformation',
          toolCallId: toolCall.toolCallId,
          output: cities[Math.floor(Math.random() * cities.length)],
        });
      } catch (err) {
        addToolError({
          tool: 'getWeatherInformation',
          toolCallId: toolCall.toolCallId,
          errorText: "Failed to get weather information",
        });
      }
    }
  },
});
```

title: feat(provider/anthropic): add web fetch tool support
body:
## Background

[Anthropic provider has server-side web fetch tool support](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool), which allows Claude to retrieve full content from web pages and PDF documents. This tool complements the existing web search functionality by enabling direct content fetching from specified URLs.

## Summary

Added support for server-side web fetch tool with the following capabilities:

- **Fetches content from web pages and PDFs** with automatic text extraction
- **Requires beta header**: `anthropic-beta: web-fetch-2025-09-10`
- **Configurable parameters**:
  - `max_uses`: Limits the number of web fetches per request
  - `allowed_domains`/`blocked_domains`: Domain filtering for security
  - `citations`: Enable citation of specific document passages
  - `max_content_tokens`: Restricts total content length

## Implementation Details

- Created `webFetch_20250910` tool factory following the existing pattern for provider-defined tools
- Automatic beta header injection when the tool is detected
- Full support for both streaming and non-streaming responses
- Proper handling of tool results with citation support
- TypeScript types for input/output schemas using Zod validation

## Security Considerations

As noted in the [Anthropic documentation](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool#security-considerations):
- The web fetch tool should be used cautiously in environments processing untrusted input alongside sensitive data due to potential data exfiltration risks
- Domain filtering capabilities (`allowed_domains`/`blocked_domains`) help mitigate security concerns
- The tool only fetches URLs explicitly provided by users or from previous search/fetch results

## Manual Verification

- Tested the Anthropic Messages API with web fetch tool
- Verified the current AI SDK doesn't support `anthropic.tools.webFetch_20250910()`
- Tested the implementation with local build using all three example files
- Confirmed proper beta header injection and tool result handling

## Tasks

- [x] Tests have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Documentation has been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] A _patch_ changeset for relevant packages has been added (for bug fixes / features - run `pnpm changeset` in the project root)
- [x] Formatting issues have been fixed (run `pnpm prettier-fix` in the project root)

## Examples Added

Three comprehensive examples demonstrating the web fetch tool usage:

1. **Basic web fetch** (`examples/ai-core/src/generate-text/anthropic-web-fetch.ts`):
   - Shows basic usage with `generateText`
   - Demonstrates citation support
   - Includes domain filtering

2. **Streaming web fetch** (`examples/ai-core/src/stream-text/anthropic-web-fetch.ts`):
   - Demonstrates streaming responses with `streamText`
   - Shows how to handle tool results after streaming completes
   - Includes error handling for failed fetches

3. **Combined web search and fetch** (`examples/ai-core/src/generate-text/anthropic-web-search-fetch.ts`):
   - Demonstrates using both `webSearch` and `webFetch` tools together
   - Shows how tools can work in tandem for comprehensive web information gathering
   - Includes detailed tool usage logging

## Testing

Added comprehensive tests in `anthropic-prepare-tools.test.ts`:
- Verifies tool configuration with all parameters
- Confirms beta header injection
- Tests tool type mapping

## Related Issues

No existing issues found specifically requesting web_fetch tool support. This PR adds a new capability to match Anthropic's latest API features.

title: RFC: Pass addToolResult into onToolCall callback
body:
<!--
Welcome to contributing to AI SDK! We're excited to see your changes.

We suggest you read the following contributing guide we've created before submitting:

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

## Background

This is a request for comment with a potential solution for an issue we've been seeing around tool calling.

We have an application that utilizes `onToolCall` to handle client side processing of tools, these are potentially long running and block the agent conversation until completion.

```ts
const { messages, sendMessage, addToolResult } = useChat({
  transport: new DefaultChatTransport({
    api: '/api/chat',
  }),

  sendAutomaticallyWhen: lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls,

  // run client-side tools that are automatically executed:
  async onToolCall({ toolCall }) {
    // Check if it's a dynamic tool first for proper type narrowing
    if (toolCall.dynamic) {
      return;
    }

    if (toolCall.toolName === 'getWeatherInformation') {
      // Long running task
      const weather = await getWeatherInformation(toolCall.input);

      // No await - avoids potential deadlocks
      addToolResult({
        tool: 'getWeatherInformation',
        toolCallId: toolCall.toolCallId,
        output: cities[Math.floor(Math.random() * cities.length)],
      });
    }
  },
});
```

We also support the user canceling the conversation mid flow using `chat.stop()`. This works well in most standard cases as the stream is aborted and the `sendAutomaticallyWhen()` check in the `makeRequest` call is skipped.

However if we have a long running tool, it's possible that the tool will return _after_ the cancellation happens.

The tool itself is not aware of the response stream nor of the cancellation so in the above case the `addToolResult` call will update `messages` with stale data and write that stale data to the currently active response if it exists. It will also then call `sendMessage()` with the stale data initiating a new conversation.

The end result for the user is that the conversation appears canceled and then suddenly the agent responds a short while later when the tool completes due to the additional `sendMessage` call in `addToolResult()`.

We currently work around this by maintaining our own state for canceled messages and suppress the `addToolResult` call in `onToolCall`:

```ts
  async onToolCall({ toolCall }) {
    // cancellation.promise resolves when `stop()` is called so that the tool
    // call doesn't block the stream.
    return Promise.race([cancellation.promise, () => {
     // Check if it's a dynamic tool first for proper type narrowing
     if (toolCall.dynamic) {
       return;
     }

     if (toolCall.toolName === 'getWeatherInformation') {
       // Long running task
       const weather = await getWeatherInformation(toolCall.input);

       if (!cancellation.isCanceled) {
        // No await - avoids potential deadlocks
        addToolResult({
          tool: 'getWeatherInformation',
          toolCallId: toolCall.toolCallId,
          output: weather,
        });
       }
     }
    }])
  },
```

## Summary

This PR adds two new additional arguments to `onToolCall` the `addToolResult` function bound to the currently active response and the `AbortSignal` associated with the active response.

The `addToolResult` call will not run if the response stream associated with the current `onToolCall` call is terminated.

The `signal` is provided so that users can implement their own tear down code if needed if the stream is canceled.

```ts
  async onToolCall({ toolCall, addToolResult, signal }) {
    // Check if it's a dynamic tool first for proper type narrowing
    if (toolCall.dynamic) {
      return;
    }

    if (toolCall.toolName === 'getWeatherInformation') {
      // Signal can be used potentially in multi step flows...
      const location = await getLocation(toolCall.input);
      if (signal?.aborted) {
        return;
      }

      // Long running task, can tear down if signal is aborted...
      const weather = await getWeatherInformation(location, { signal });

      const summary = await summarize(weather);

      // Regardless, result will now be a no-op if signal is aborted.
      addToolResult({
        tool: 'getWeatherInformation',
        toolCallId: toolCall.toolCallId,
        output: weather,
      });
    }
  },
```

title: build: add `"type": "module"` to `package.json`
body:
It is recommended to mention `"type": "module"` explicitly since we are using ESM everywhere. Otherwise it incurs some performance issue. Node.js doc says, "Syntax detection should have no performance impact on CommonJS modules, but it incurs a slight performance penalty for ES modules; add "type": "module" to the nearest parent package.json file to eliminate the performance cost. "

https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v20.19.0#module-syntax-detection-is-now-enabled-by-default

title: feature(ai): add onToolOutput callback
body:
## Background

Added onToolOutput, similar to onToolCall. This is missing in cases where you want to have some effect run on the frontend once the tool call has results.

This addresses the feature request in [issue #6080](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/6080).

## Summary

Added a new `onToolOutput` callback to the `useChat` hook that fires when a tool call returns an output. 

Note: I named it `onToolOutput` to be consistent with the existing naming patterns in the codebase, but it could also be called `onToolResult` if that's preferred. Let me know which naming convention ya'll prefer.

## Manual Verification

I verified the implementation works end-to-end by:

1. **Testing the callback execution**: Created a test chat instance with an `onToolOutput` callback and verified it gets called when tool outputs are received during streaming
2. **Verifying tool output data structure**: Confirmed the callback receives the correct tool output object with all expected properties (toolCallId, toolName, input, output, etc.)
3. **Testing with different tool types**: Verified the callback works with both static and dynamic tools
4. **Type safety validation**: Ensured TypeScript types are properly inferred for different tool configurations
5. **Integration testing**: Confirmed the callback integrates properly with the existing streaming and message processing pipeline

title: docs: change provider options from azure to openai
body:
## Background

The `@ai-sdk/azure` package's documentation for the embed function was misleading. It instructed users to pass provider-specific options using the azure key within the providerOptions object (e.g., `providerOptions: { azure: { dimensions: 512 } })`. However, the implementation only recognized the openai key, which is the standard for the underlying API. This inconsistency caused confusion and wasted time for users attempting to configure Azure embeddings.

## Summary

This pull request updates the documentation for the `@ai-sdk/azure` package to correctly reflect how provider-specific options for the embed function should be passed. The documentation now explicitly states that the `providerOptions` key should be openai, aligning with the existing code implementation.

title: feat(codemod): add usechat input state transformation for v5
body:
## background

the v5 migration removes managed input state from the usechat hook. users need to manually manage input state with usestate instead of relying on the built-in input and handleinputchange from usechat. without this codemod, users would need to manually update every usechat usage in their codebase

## summary

- added codemod to transform usechat destructuring patterns
- removes input and handleinputchange from usechat
- adds usestate for local input management
- replaces handleinputchange with inline setters

## verification

tested with real-world patterns including aliased destructuring, partial extraction, and function-scoped replacements. all tests pass

## tasks

- [x] created replace-usechat-input-with-state codemod
- [x] handled import alias preservation
- [x] added function-scoped identifier replacement
- [x] created test fixtures for all edge cases
- [x] integrated into v5 upgrade bundle

title: feat(codemod): add usechat api to transport transformation
body:
## background

the usechat hook api prop has been replaced with a transport prop in v5 to provide more flexibility and control over how messages are sent and received. users upgrading from v4 to v5 need a codemod to automatically transform their existing usechat api usage to the new transport pattern

## summary

- created codemod to transform `useChat({ api: string })` to `useChat({ transport: new DefaultChatTransport({ api: string }) })`
- handles both `ai` and `@ai-sdk/react` imports
- supports all property types (string literals, variables, template literals)
- preserves existing properties alongside the transformed transport

## verification

tested transformation with various patterns including string literals, variables, and template literals. all existing tests pass

## tasks

- [x] created replace-usechat-api-with-transport codemod
- [x] added test fixtures
- [x] integrated into v5 upgrade bundle
- [x] verified codemod works with real examples

title: fix(ai): only parse experimental_output in generateText when finishReason is stop
body:
## Background

When using `generateText` with both tools and `experimental_output`, there was a bug where tool results could reference tool calls that weren't found, causing runtime errors of `AI_NoObjectGeneratedError`. This occurred because the code was trying to parse the `content` output of the last message to match the schema of `experimental_output`, but since the LLM returned with a `tool-calls` finish reason the `content` was empty, or misformated, and this is a valid response.

## Summary

Added a condition to only parse when the finish reason is 'stop'. This avoid unnecessary parsing of tool call responses and errors for LLM that return with `content` as null when finished with a tool call (e.g. openai models).

## Manual Verification

Tested with a `generateText` on gpt-4o-mini with a call that uses both experimental output parsing and tool calls:
1. When generation finishes with tool calls, output parsing is skipped and no errors occur
2. When generation finishes with regular text (not tool calls), output parsing works as expected

## Related Issues

Fixes https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/8009

Validating LLM outputs isn't only about correctness, it's about extracting signals. Scorers make that possible

this implementation:
- includes scoring results in the final step response
- helps when running evals (e.g. [Evalite scorers](https://www.evalite.dev/guides/scorers))
- makes it easier to validate interaction + user intention across agent <> tools
- opens the door to using other LLMs as evaluators [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.02863)

## Summary

- adds a first version of scorers support in `streamText`
- runs defined scorers on `tool-result` parts
- results are exposed in `onStepFinish({ scorers })`
- includes an example (examples/ai-core/src/stream-text/gateway-scorers.ts)

this is a poc, only wired into `streamText` and still missing docs, tests, and broader integration

## Manual Verification

`bun run ./stream-text/gateway-scorers.ts`

body:
<!--
Welcome to contributing to AI SDK! We're excited to see your changes.

We suggest you read the following contributing guide we've created before submitting:

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

## Background

Twelve Labs provides state-of-the-art multimodal video understanding models that can analyze, search, and create embeddings from video content. This integration brings Twelve Labs' advanced video AI capabilities to the Vercel AI SDK, enabling developers to build powerful video-aware applications.

## Summary

  Added a new provider (`@ai-sdk/twelvelabs`) that brings video AI capabilities to the Vercel AI SDK:

  **Core Features:**
  - **Video Analysis**: Ask questions about video content and get natural language responses (e.g., "What happens in this video?", "How many people are visible?")
  - **Video Search**: Search through video content using natural language queries (e.g., "Find moments where someone is playing basketball")
  - **Video & Text Embeddings**: Convert videos and text descriptions into numerical representations for similarity matching, search, and retrieval
  - **Multiple Input Methods**: Works with video URLs, local video files, or previously processed videos

  **Technical Implementation:**
  - Uses two specialized AI models under the hood - one optimized for understanding/Q&A (`pegasus1.2`) and another for search/embeddings (`marengo2.7`)
  - Automatically manages the infrastructure needed to process and store videos
  - Supports streaming responses for real-time video analysis
  - Returns video IDs that can be reused for faster follow-up questions (avoiding re-processing)
  
  
## Manual Verification
  
Comprehensive testing was performed with real video files:

  1. **Local Video Processing**:
     - Successfully processed local MP4 video files
     - Received accurate descriptions of video content
     - Demonstrated ability to reuse processed videos for multiple questions
     - Confirmed significant performance improvement when reusing video IDs (no re-upload needed)

  2. **Complete Feature Testing**:
     - Verified video upload and processing from both URLs and local files
     - Tested search functionality across video content
     - Validated both text and video embedding generation
     - Tested similarity matching between embeddings
     - Confirmed proper separation of Q&A and search functionalities
     - All error scenarios handled appropriately

  Key validation points:
  - Videos are automatically processed and indexed on first use
  - Video IDs are properly returned for reuse in subsequent requests
  - Search feature finds a relevant video
  - Both text and video embeddings work correctly for similarity matching
  - Streaming responses work correctly for long-form analysis
  - Processing metadata (timing, IDs) is correctly exposed to developers

title: fix(provider/openai): change the "incomplete_details" key from nullable to nullish for better openai compatibility
body:
## Background

As reported in [#8835](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/8835),  
`incomplete_details` was defined as `.nullable()`, forcing `null` instead of allowing omission.  
This caused validation issues when the property was simply missing.

## Summary

Changed schema:

```diff
-    incomplete_details: z.object({ reason: z.string() }).nullable(),
+    incomplete_details: z.object({ reason: z.string() }).nullish(),
````

This matches runtime behavior: `incomplete_details` may be omitted, or provided as an object.
`null` remains accepted as well.

## Manual Verification

* Verified build passes
* Objects with omitted `incomplete_details` now validate correctly
* Objects with `incomplete_details: { reason: "..." }` validate correctly
* `incomplete_details: null` still accepted

body:
This makes it more convenient to implement custom `ChatTransport` implementations.

<!--
Welcome to contributing to AI SDK! We're excited to see your changes.

We suggest you read the following contributing guide we've created before submitting:

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

## Background

While implementing a custom `useChat` transport, I noticed these are missing from the `ai` package exports:

* The `parseJsonEventStream()` function. I could grab this from the `@ai-sdk/provider-util` package directly, but since the `ai` package is already re-exporting stuff from this package, this would be nice to have as well.
* The `uiMessageChunkSchema` zod schema is necessary for usage of `parseJsonEventStream()`.

Re-exported `parseJsonEventStream` from `@ai-sdk/provider-util`, and exported `uiMessageChunkSchema`.

title: fix(ai): update `uiMessageChunkSchema` to satisfy the `UIMessageChunk` type
body:
## Background

The `uiMessageChunkSchema` seems to be out of date with the TypeScript `UIMessageChunk` type. Consider the following code:

```ts
import { type UIMessageChunk, uiMessageChunkSchema } from "ai";

const m: UIMessageChunk = uiMessageChunkSchema.parse({
	type: "text-delta",
	delta: "Hello, world!",
	id: "123",
});
```

This was producing the following TypeScript error:

```
Type '{ type: "text-start"; id: string; providerMetadata?: SharedV2ProviderMetadata | undefined; } | { type: "text-delta"; id: string; delta: string; providerMetadata?: SharedV2ProviderMetadata | undefined; } | ... 22 more ... | { ...; }' is not assignable to type 'UIMessageChunk'.
  Type '{ type: "reasoning"; text: string; providerMetadata?: SharedV2ProviderMetadata | undefined; }' is not assignable to type 'UIMessageChunk'.
    Type '{ type: "reasoning"; text: string; providerMetadata?: SharedV2ProviderMetadata | undefined; }' is missing the following properties from type '{ type: "source-document"; sourceId: string; mediaType: string; title: string; filename?: string | undefined; providerMetadata?: SharedV2ProviderMetadata | undefined; }': sourceId, mediaType, titlets(2322)
```

## Summary

* remove unused types from schema
* add provider metadata for file
* update data type parsing to support template string

## Manual Testing

- [x] test UI example with reasoning (2 steps, OpenAI)

## Tasks

- [x] add type test
- [x] investigate expected behavior

title: feat(provider/openai): Add Code Interpreter input streaming support
body:
## Background

The OpenAI Responses API streams messages to provide delta/done updates for the `code` input to the built in Code Interpreter tool calls. The current implementation ignored these messages, so the first `tool-call` streaming message comes much later than necessary.

## Summary

Uses the `response.code_interpreter_call_code.delta` and `response.code_interpreter_call_code.done` messages from the Responses API stream to produce `tool-input-start`, `tool-input-delta`, and `tool-input-end` messages in the SDK output stream.

title: fix(react): make useChat callbacks not stale
body:
## Background

`useChat` captures the initial `onToolCall` callback via closures, offering no mechanism to refresh the callback during a chat’s lifetime. When the React component changes context/state (e.g., changing the value of a `useState` hook), `onToolCall` continues using stale values, leading to incorrect client-side tool execution and unexpected behavior. The only way to fix this was to wrap the values inside `useRef`.

## Summary

- Core (`ai`): add runtime setters on `AbstractChat` to update callbacks without recreating the chat instance:
  - `setOnToolCall`, `setOnData`, `setOnFinish`, `setOnError`, `setSendAutomaticallyWhen`.
- React (`@ai-sdk/react`): update `useChat` to call these setters inside an effect when options change, ensuring the latest callbacks are always used.
- Tests: add a regression test ensuring the latest `onToolCall` is invoked after a prop change.

## Manual Verification

- Local example with a toggle that switches the `onToolCall` implementation at runtime (simulates changed `resources` context). After the toggle, subsequent tool calls were handled by the updated callback and used the latest context values.
- Confirmed chat instances were not re-created when only callback props changed.
- Verified streaming tool calls still dispatch and complete as expected.

## Checklist

title: feat(provider/azure) : enable Responses API tool image_generation for AzureOpenAI
body:
## Background
Azure OpenAI Responses API built-in tools 'image_generation' is now available (it's preview ,not GA).
It will be available with @ai-sdk/azure provider.

### Responses API : AI Platforms comparison
Azure OpenAI Responses API built-in tools status in September 2025.

tool/AI platform | OpenAI | Microsoft Azure OpenAI
-- | -- | --
web_search_preview | ✅ Enabled(deprecated) | ❌ Not currently supported
web_search | ✅ Enabled | ❌ Not currently supported
code_interpreter | ✅ Enabled | ✅ Enabled
file_search | ✅ Enabled | ✅ Enabled
**image_generation** | ✅ **Enabled** | ✅ **Enabled(preview)**

> [!NOTE]
> The web_search is not supported in Azure OpenAI provider.
> The image_generaton is preview and streaming is not supported , input image file is not supported now.
> https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/how-to/responses?tabs=python-secure#model-support

### Responses API : @ai-sdk/openai and @ai-sdk/azure comparison
tool/ai-sdk | @ai-sdk/openai | @ai-sdk/azure
-- | -- | --
web_search_preview | ✅ Enabled(deprecated) | ❌ Not Prepared
web_search | ✅ Enabled | ❌ Not Prepared
code_interpreter | ✅ Enabled | ✅ Enabled
file_search | ✅ Enabled | ✅ Enabled
**image_generation** | ✅ **Enabled** | 🚀**Will be Enabled ( with limited functionality )**


## Summary

### how it make works.
Azure provider's image_generation is enabled like openai provider.
openai's tools image_generation is added to internal export (packages/openai/src/internal/index.ts).
And azure's tools get the implementations from import openai provider's tools.

azure.tools.imageGeneration build-in tool will be available.

``` typescript
const azure = createAzure({
  headers: {
    'x-ms-oai-image-generation-deployment': 'gpt-image-1', // use your own image model deployment
  },
});

const result = await generateText({
  model: azure.responses('gpt-4.1-mini'), // use your own deployment
  prompt: `Create an anime-like image of a cute cat waving hello.`,
  tools: {
    image_generation: azure.tools.imageGeneration({
      outputFormat: 'png',  // on azure , supported extension is png and jpeg.
      quality: 'medium',
      size: '1024x1024',
    }),
  }
});

for (const toolResult of result.staticToolResults) {
  if (toolResult.toolName === 'image_generation') {
    const base64Image = toolResult.output.result;
  }
}
```

### image_generation is Preview release (Not GA).
I found that stream mode is not supported now , so image_generation does not work on streamText function.
So add the warning in azure documents and notice comment in example code.
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/how-to/responses?tabs=python-key#image-generation-preview

<!--
Welcome to contributing to AI SDK! We're excited to see your changes.

We suggest you read the following contributing guide we've created before submitting:

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

## Background

Some deployments need to target an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (e.g. self-hosted proxy, regional gateway). The OpenAI provider currently hardcodes the API base URL, which makes this inconvenient.

## Summary

- Add support for configuring the API base URL via the `OPENAI_BASE_URL` environment variable and the `baseURL` option on the provider.
- Continue to default to `https://api.openai.com/v1` when not provided.
- Applies consistently across chat, completion, responses, embeddings, image, transcription, and speech models.

## Manual Verification

- Set `OPENAI_BASE_URL` to a custom endpoint (e.g. `https://api.openai-proxy.example/v1`).
- Initialize via `createOpenAI()` and call `openai.responses(/* modelId */)`; requests target the configured host.
- Unset the env var and omit `baseURL`; requests fall back to `https://api.openai.com/v1`.
- Also verified that an explicit `baseURL` option takes precedence over the env var.

title: docs(examples): replace 'latest' with specific versions in package.json
body:
<!--
Welcome to contributing to AI SDK! We're excited to see your changes.

We suggest you read the following contributing guide we've created before submitting:

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

## Background

This PR addresses [issue #9019](https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/9019) which identified that multiple `package.json` files in the examples directory were using `"latest"` as version specifiers for dependencies. Using `"latest"` is problematic because:

- It's non-deterministic (different developers may get different versions)
- It can cause CI/CD failures due to unexpected version changes
- It makes debugging difficult when issues arise from version mismatches
- It goes against best practices for dependency management

## Summary

Replaced all instances of `"latest"` with specific semantic version ranges in examples package.json files:

- **Next.js**: `"latest"` → `"^15.5.4"` (11 instances)
- **@vercel/functions**: `"latest"` → `"^3.1.0"` (1 instance)

**Files modified:**
- `examples/next/package.json`
- `examples/next-agent/package.json`
- `examples/next-fastapi/package.json`
- `examples/next-google-vertex/package.json`
- `examples/next-langchain/package.json`
- `examples/next-openai/package.json`
- `examples/next-openai-kasada-bot-protection/package.json`
- `examples/next-openai-pages/package.json`
- `examples/next-openai-telemetry/package.json`
- `examples/next-openai-telemetry-sentry/package.json`
- `examples/next-openai-upstash-rate-limits/package.json`

## Manual Verification

### 1. Identified the problem
```bash
# Found all instances of "latest" in package.json files
grep -r '"latest"' --include="package.json" .
```

**Result:** Found 12 instances across 11 files in examples directory.

### 2. Obtained current versions
```bash
# Checked current stable versions
npm view next version
npm view @vercel/functions version
```

**Result:** 
- Next.js: `15.5.4`
- @vercel/functions: `3.1.0`

### 3. Applied changes systematically
Used semantic versioning with `^` prefix to allow compatible updates while maintaining stability.

### 4. Verified formatting
```bash
# Applied code formatting
pnpm prettier-fix
```

### 5. Confirmed all changes
```bash
# Verified no "latest" remains in examples package.json files
grep -r '"latest"' --include="package.json" examples/ || echo "No 'latest' found in examples package.json files"
```

**Result:** `No 'latest' found in examples package.json files` ✅

### 6. Final verification
```bash
# Checked specific files to confirm changes
grep -A1 -B1 '"next":' examples/next/package.json examples/next-openai/package.json examples/next-openai-kasada-bot-protection/package.json
```

**Result:** All files now show `"next": "^15.5.4"` instead of `"next": "latest"`

## Checklist

Do not edit this list. Leave items unchecked that don't apply. If you need to track subtasks, create a new "## Tasks" section

-->

title: feat(ai): add retry support to onError callback in generateObject/streamObject
body:
<!--
Welcome to contributing to AI SDK! We're excited to see your changes.

We suggest you read the following contributing guide we've created before submitting:

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

## Background

currently `maxRetries` only handles model api errors. However, `generateObject` and `streamObject` can fail for other reasons (e.g. schema validation errors, JSON parsing errors). this pr enables developers to implement custom retry logic for these cases

## Summary

adds support for custom retry logic via the onError callback in `generateObject` and `streamObject`

- added `retry` function to `onError` callback that accepts partial options: `{ ...originalOptions, ...newOptions }`
- wired `onError` callback into the `parseAndValidateObjectResultWithRepair` catch block to enable retries on schema validation failures
- extracted `StreamObjectOptions` to `stream-object-options.ts`
- extracted `GenerateObjectOptions` to `generate-object-options.ts`
- created `StreamObjectReturnType` helper type for better type inference
- added `onError` parameter doc to `generate-object` reference (prev undocumented)
- updated `onError` parameter doc in `stream-object` to include `retry` function

example usage:
```ts
const result = await generateObject({
  model: 'xai/grok-3-beta',
  schema: z.object({
      recipe: z.object({
        name: z.string(),
        ingredients: z.array(
          z.object({
            name: z.string(),
            amount: z.string(),
          }),
        ),
        steps: z.array(z.string()),
      }),
  }),
  prompt: 'Generate a lasagna recipe',
  onError: async ({ error, retry }) => {
    // Retry with adjusted temperature
    if (shouldRetry(error)) {
      return await retry({ temperature: 0.5 });
    }
  },
});
```

tested basic retry functionality with `generateObject` and `streamObject`

title: feat(ai): add MCP resources support
body:
## Summary

Implements full Model Context Protocol (MCP) resources support in the AI SDK, enabling applications to discover and access structured information sources from MCP servers.

Addresses issue #6294

## Features

### Core API
- `listResources()` - List available resources with pagination support
- `listResourceTemplates()` - Discover dynamic resource URI templates  
- `readResource()` - Fetch resource content (supports string URI or `{uri}` object)
- `includeResources` option - Expose resources as callable AI tools

### Implementation
- Added `Resource`, `ResourceTemplate`, and `ReadResourceResult` type definitions
- Extended `MCPClient` interface with resource methods
- Implemented resource-to-tool conversion with automatic parameter extraction
- Direct resources become zero-parameter tools (`resource_${name}`)
- Resource templates become parameterized tools (`resource_template_${name}`)
- RFC 6570 URI template parameter parsing for dynamic resources
- Full pagination support for listing operations
- API aligned with MCP TypeScript SDK reference implementation

### Usage Patterns

**RAG Pattern (Resources as Context):**
```typescript
const result = await mcpClient.listResources();
const content = await mcpClient.readResource(result.resources[0].uri);

// Include in prompt
const response = await generateText({
  model: openai('gpt-4'),
  prompt: `Context: ${content.contents[0].text}\n\nQuestion: ...`
});
```

**Agentic Pattern (Resources as Tools):**
```typescript
const tools = await mcpClient.tools({ includeResources: true });

const result = await streamText({
  model: openai('gpt-4'),
  tools, // AI can now call resource tools
  maxSteps: 5,
  prompt: 'Fetch and analyze the data'
});
```

## Testing

- Comprehensive unit tests for all resource operations
- Mock transport extended to support resource endpoints
- Real-world integration tests with `nostr-explore-mcp` server
- Working examples demonstrating both RAG and agentic patterns

## Documentation

- Updated MCP tools documentation with resource usage patterns
- Examples for listing, reading, and using resources as tools
- Guidance on RAG vs tool-based approaches
- 4 working example files with live MCP servers

## Exported Types

- `experimental_MCPResource`
- `experimental_MCPResourceTemplate`  
- `experimental_MCPReadResourceResult`

## Files Changed

**Core Implementation:**
- `packages/ai/src/tool/mcp/types.ts` - Resource type definitions
- `packages/ai/src/tool/mcp/mcp-client.ts` - Client methods & conversion logic
- `packages/ai/src/tool/mcp/mock-mcp-transport.ts` - Mock support for testing
- `packages/ai/src/tool/index.ts` - Public API exports

**Tests:**
- `packages/ai/src/tool/mcp/mcp-client.test.ts` - Unit tests

**Documentation:**
- `content/docs/03-ai-sdk-core/16-mcp-tools.mdx` - Usage guide

**Examples:**
- `packages/ai/examples/mcp-resources-example.ts` - Basic operations
- `packages/ai/examples/mcp-resources-read-template.ts` - Template reading
- `packages/ai/examples/mcp-resources-simple.ts` - Minimal example
- `packages/ai/examples/mcp-resources-with-streamtext.ts` - Full agentic pattern
- `packages/ai/examples/README-resources.md` - Example docs

## Compatibility

This implementation is fully backward compatible and adds no breaking changes. The `includeResources` parameter is optional and defaults to `false`.

body: ## Background The Code Interpreter can create files through Python execution. OpenAI provides an API that allows downloading files from the Code Interpreter container. To use this API, both the `container_id` and `file_id` are required. Therefore, the AI SDK needs to support returning the [`container-file-citation`](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses/object#responses/object-output-output-message-content-output-text-annotations-container-file-citation) annotation to provide these IDs to the client. Reference: - [OpenAI API – Get the file contents](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/container-files/retrieveContainerFileContent) - [OpenAI API – About `container-file-citation`](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses/object#responses/object-output-output-message-content-output-text-annotations-container-file-citation) This PR enables handling of the `container_file_citation` annotation so that the `container_id` and `file_id` can be retrieved and returned to the client. ## Summary This PR enables returning the parameters required by the OpenAI **Container File API** for files generated by the **Code Interpreter**. Developers can continue using `useChat` and `streamText` as before, but the output may now include the `container-file-citation` annotation and a new `source-execution-file` entry. This makes it possible to replace text references with actual download URLs, or to provide link-based UIs powered by `source-execution-file`. Users can simply click the link to retrieve the generated file, allowing the AI SDK to seamlessly handle various file formats (e.g., Excel). ### DEMO - GIF animation - examples/next-openai/src/app/test-openai-code-interpreter-download-files - http://localhost:3000/test-openai-code-interpreter-download-files ![codeinterpreterdownloadfile](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0e3d507-dbe9-47ef-bff7-d2a3afae1899) ## Receiving `container_file_citation` in `TextUIPart` The client can receive the OpenAI annotation `container_file_citation` using the TextUIPart's providerMetadata. This PR retrieves the `container_file_citation` annotation from `providerMetadata` and replaces the corresponding text message according to a defined rule. By further rendering it through markdown (e.g., **Streamdown**), the output enables users to directly click and download the files generated by the Code Interpreter. This approach improves usability — instead of copying raw sandbox paths or API URLs, users can now access the generated files with a single click, resulting in a much better UX. ``` { type: 'text', text: 'I have created an Excel file containing the names of 10 historical figures. You can download it here:\n' + '\n' + '[Download the Excel file](sandbox:/mnt/data/historical_figures.xlsx)', providerMetadata: { openai: { itemId: 'msg_09fa2bb0f5d25ded0068e7ce98cdfc8195853725f2bf424486', annotations: [ { type: 'container_file_citation', container_id: 'cntr_68e7ce8aef948190a3447822efbd111c0745ba41b6f16e8a', file_id: 'cfile_68e7ce9ba01c8191a81ff3ce590dfc44', filename: 'historical_figures.xlsx', start_index: 129, end_index: 170 } ] } } }, ``` #### Visualization Example (Comparison Table) Below is a comparison of plain text vs. markdown rendering (Streamdown). When the `container_file_citation` annotation is applied, users can click to download the file directly — improving both **functionality** and **UX**. > [!CAUTION] > This PR adds the `container_file_citation` annotation to providerMetadata. > Similarly, `file_citation` and `url_citation` annotations are also attached in the same way. > These annotations are currently included even when `sendSources` is set to false. > If reviewers believe this behavior should be adjusted before merging, I’ll be happy to update the implementation accordingly. ## `source-execution-file`: Independent Download UI A third type, `source-execution-file`, can be created in SourceUIPart to build a download UI that is independent of the text. ProviderMetadata for this purpose has also been defined. #### `source-execution-file` (Independent Download UI) When using **`streamText`**, a new source part with `type: "execution-file"` is generated. This part enables creating a **clickable download UI** that is independent from the text message itself. For example, the Excel file generated by the Code Interpreter can be shown as a **blue download button**, allowing users to easily obtain the file without interacting with the text content. #### Example Output ``` { type: 'source', sourceType: 'execution-file', id: 'pgDscAT78wrTK3dG', providerMetadata: { openai: { containerId: 'cntr_68e7e2fb0e408190b9a122b2b2d6ea2d0e937059125f30cc', fileId: 'cfile_68e7e312edbc8191a08252ebc0791a06', filename: 'historical_figures.xlsx' } } } ``` #### Visualization Example For example , like this button. The blue button appears at the end of the text message. ## Parsing `providerMetadata` with Zod A Zod schema has been introduced to safely parse the `providerMetadata` of each UI part and extract the required information. This ensures type safety and prevents runtime errors when handling provider-specific metadata. For example, the `TextUIPart` uses the `container_file_citation` annotation metadata, while the `SourceExecutionFileUIPart` extracts file-related parameters such as `containerId`, `fileId`, and `filename`. https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/1c7953a936fff88169ac74fc02820336e89538c8/packages/openai/src/responses/openai-responses-api.ts#L706-L719 A zod parse for `source-file-citation` example. https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/1c7953a936fff88169ac74fc02820336e89538c8/examples/next-openai/app/test-openai-code-interpreter-download-files/container-file-citation-download-button.tsx#L11-L27 ## Available in both `@ai-sdk/openai` and `@ai-sdk/azure`. Similar to the OpenAI implementation, a Zod schema is also provided for **Azure OpenAI**. #### `z.union` Unified Zod Schema for Multiple Providers This approach helps handle provider-specific metadata safely and consistently, enabling appropriate logic for each provider. https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/ee8d88b25f71cdd724b549c94e5efb181ebbc6eb/examples/next-openai/app/test-azure-code-interpreter-download-files/message-text-with-download-link.tsx#L10-L26 ## Example: File Download Route for Next.js Since the actual file download is handled through **native fetching** from OpenAI’s official API, an example `route.ts` file has been added for Next.js to demonstrate how the download endpoint can be implemented. You can see the example implementation here: https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/1c7953a936fff88169ac74fc02820336e89538c8/examples/next-openai/app/api/chat-openai-code-interpreter-download-files/%5Bcontainer%5D/%5Bfile%5D/route.ts#L32-L38 ## Manual Verification ### ai-core - [x] src\generate-text\openai-responses-code-interpreter-download-files.ts - [x] src\stream-text\openai-responses-code-interpreter-download-files.ts - [x] src\generate-text\azure-responses-code-interpreter-download-files.ts - [x] src\stream-text\azure-responses-code-interpreter-download-files.ts ### example/next-openai - [x] OpenAI http://localhost:3000/test-openai-code-interpreter-download-files - [x] Azure OpenAI http://localhost:3000/test-azure-code-interpreter-download-files - when the test, run `pnpm add clsx tailwind-merge streamdown` and fix comments in`additional-dependencies.tsx` file. - input example `Create an Excel file with the names of 10 historical figures. Run it immediately. No questions allowed.` ## Checklist - [ ] Tests have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features) - [ ] Documentation has been added / updated (for bug fixes / features) - [ ] A _patch_ changeset for relevant packages has been added (for bug fixes / features - run `pnpm changeset` in the project root) - [ ] Formatting issues have been fixed (run `pnpm prettier-fix` in the project root) - [ ] I have reviewed this pull request (self-review) > [!NOTE] > This PR depends on `SharedV3ProviderMetadata`. ## Future Work > [!CAUTION] > (Repost) > This PR adds the `container_file_citation` annotation to providerMetadata. > Similarly, `file_citation` and `url_citation` annotations are also attached in the same way. > These annotations are currently included even when `sendSources` is set to false. > While this behavior may change before the PR is merged, it is noted as Future Work for now. ## Related Issues

title: feat(provider/amazon-bedrock): Support user provided filenames in amazon-bedrock-provider
body:
<!--
Welcome to contributing to AI SDK! We're excited to see your changes.

We suggest you read the following contributing guide we've created before submitting:

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

## Background

I noticed that when using the `FilePart` type to send files to the Bedrock provider, there's currently no support for passing through the `filename` field — even though it's part of the interface.

In the current implementation, the document name is always auto-generated:

```ts
let documentCounter = 0;
const generateDocumentName = () => `document-${++documentCounter}`;

bedrockContent.push({
  document: {
    format: getBedrockDocumentFormat(part.mediaType),
    name: generateDocumentName(), // filename is ignored
    source: { bytes: convertToBase64(part.data) },
    ...(enableCitations && {
      citations: { enabled: true },
    }),
  },
});
```

Since the `FilePart` interface already includes an optional `filename`:

```ts
interface FilePart {
  ...
  filename?: string;
  ...
}
```

It would be great if the Bedrock provider used the `filename` value (when provided) instead of always generating a default name.


This allows users to provide meaningful filenames when needed, while still falling back to the generated one if no `filename` is supplied.

Our team noticed that when we reference documents by filename in the chat message the LLM doesn't recognize them as it only has the sanitized name. This was also confusing to us as we provided the filenames to the LLM but they were getting silently sanitized. 

<!-- Why was this change necessary? -->

## Summary

<!-- What did you change? -->

Here is my proposed change to the code:
```ts
name: part.filename ?? generateDocumentName(),
```

## Manual Verification

Tested to see if when the request has a custom name that the ai can see the custom named file.

title: feat(provider/azure): default api-version has changed from preview to v1
body:
## Background
Microsoft Azure OpenAI released an OpenAI-compatible endpoint in May 2025, with the initial api-version being `preview`.
In August 2025, the latest api-version, `v1`, was released, with earlier api-versions being treated as previous versions.
This pull request aims to update the `@ai-sdk/azure` package to work with the latest `v1` version and report test results.


The latest version is expected to ensure that future updates to the Responses API and other APIs are not left behind.
For Example,[Not currently supported](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/how-to/responses?tabs=python-key#responses-api):
- The web search tool
- Image generation using multi-turn editing and streaming - coming soon
- Images can't be uploaded as a file and then referenced as input. Coming soon.

body:
## Background

When using OpenAI's web search tool, I noticed that `providerExecuted` field is unset on `tool-input-start` chunks.

`tool-input-start` chunks have a `providerExecuted` field which should represent whether a tool is executed by the provider or not. This field is correctly set to true on Anthropic's provider executed tools (on `tool-input-start` chunks) but that is not the case with OpenAI.

## Summary

Add providerExecuted flag to tool start chunks for web search, etc.

Fixes  https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/9180

title: fix(ai): `MCPClientError` had to be made JSONRPC structure compliant
body:
## Background

The JSONRPC spec (for MCP) has a `data` field which is important for doing [x402 over mcp](https://github.com/coinbase/x402/blob/main/specs/transports/mcp.md#payment-required-signaling)
The AI-SDK didn't expose `error.data`, only `error.message`

## Summary

added the `data` property to the MCPClientError to capture the `error.data` from the response

## Manual Verification

Added unit test

title: feat(ai): enable experimental_context override in prepareStep
body:
## Problem
Currently, `experimental_context` cannot be overridden in prepareStep(), unlike other properties such as model, toolChoice, and activeTools. This prevents dynamic context injection per step.

## Use Case
At [Twenty](https://github.com/twentyhq/twenty), we're building multi-agent systems where each agent has a unique role with different permissions (field access, row-level filtering, object access, etc.). With dozens of agents and hundreds of fields or millions of rows, we can't pre-generate all possible tool combinations. Instead, we use generic tools (e.g., createCompany, createLead) and inject role-specific context at runtime based on the intersection of the agent role and user role. I tried to find a better option than this but using `experimental_context`  was the best lead I could find to pass the agent's role dynamically to the function call.

## Solution
Added experimental_context to PrepareStepResult type, allowing it to be overridden per step:

title: chore(ai): load zod schemas lazily
body:
## Background

Cloudflare workers with AI SDK 5 and Zod 4.0 are exceeding their allowed startup time (see https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/issues/10723). CPU profiles indicated that this might be related to Zod schema initialization on import. Other developers have reported initialization time changes with Zod 4.x (see https://dev.to/dzakh/zod-v4-17x-slower-and-why-you-should-care-1m1 )

## Summary

Make zod schema initialization and JSON schema generation lazy. This removes it from the startup time and eliminates unnecessary initialization/schema generation, e.g. for unused model types.

Used in `ai` and `@ai-sdk/openai` packages.

Changed `import { z } from 'zod/v4'` to `import * as z from 'zod/v4'`

### Startup Performance Measurements

```ts
const t0 = performance.now();
const { openai } = await import('@ai-sdk/openai');
const t1 = performance.now();

console.log(`Import @ai-sdk/openai: ${(t1 - t0).toFixed(1)} ms`);
```

* `ai`: before ~27ms, after ~25ms, compiled ~16ms
* `@ai-sdk/openai`: before ~37ms, after ~30ms, compiled ~25ms

## Manual Verification

- [x] run `examples/ai-core/src/stream-text/openai.ts`
- [x] run `examples/next-openai` http://localhost:3000/test-openai-code-interpreter

## Future Work

* Use lazy schema loading in other provider packages
* Remove exposing zod schemas to end users

## Related Issues

https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/issues/10723

<!--
Welcome to contributing to AI SDK! We're excited to see your changes.

We suggest you read the following contributing guide we've created before submitting:

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

## Background
Users migrating from v4 to v5 are encountering errors when using text files (`text/plain`, `text/markdown`, etc.) as file attachments. In v4, `experimental_attachments` appeared to work with text files, but in v5 the SDK correctly enforces the underlying API limitations.


<!-- Why was this change necessary? -->

## Summary
Added a warning note in the "Attachments → File Parts" section of the v5 migration guide to clarify:
- OpenAI/Azure OpenAI only support `image/*`, `application/pdf`, and `audio/*` as file parts
- Text files are NOT supported as file parts
- How to migrate: read text file content and send as `text` parts instead

Example migration path:
```tsx
// Instead of this:
{ type: 'file', data: buffer, mediaType: 'text/plain' }

// Do this:
{ type: 'text', text: buffer.toString('utf-8') }
```

title: feat(ai): rootSpan flag for telemetry options
body:
## Background

The reason to propose this is that currently I'm having a hard time getting telemetry to show up correctly in langfuse while using effect.

Because the stream returned by stream operations exists outside the lifecycle of the calling function, traces get reported out of order, and ultimately certain attributes that should be made available to the root span never make it.

So forcing the ai traces to be isolated isi the only way I've been able to sort of solve it.

## Summary

Adds a new flag `rootSpan` to `experimental_telemetry` that instructs to create a root span (detached from any parent) during the execution. Defaults to false keeping the current behavior.

## Manual Verification

Tested a local build with my existing app

title: fix(provider/amazon-bedrock): ensure reasoningConfig works with additionalModelRequestFields
body:
## Background

Spreading providerOptions.bedrock into the request allowed user additionalModelRequestFields to overwrite the computed map that includes thinking derived from reasoningConfig.

## Summary

Excluded both reasoningConfig and additionalModelRequestFields from the spread into the Bedrock request. Always use the internally merged bedrockOptions.additionalModelRequestFields, which combines user fields with the derived thinking (derived values take precedence on conflict).

## Manual Verification

Used the repro script in #9312 and added two tests:
- doGenerate: merges user additionalModelRequestFields with derived thinking.
- doStream: merges user additionalModelRequestFields with derived thinking.

title: chore(provider/anthropic): lazy schema loading
body:
## Background

In #9275, lazy schema loading to reduce package import times was introduced for `ai` and `@ai-sdk/openai`. Similar changes need to be made to all providers.

## Summary

Load zod schemas in the `@ai-sdk/anthropic` provider lazily.

## Manual Verification

In `examples/ai-core` (need to run tsc every time there is a change you want to benchmark):

```sh
pnpm tsc -b
node build/benchmark/anthropic-load-time.js
``` 

Before: ~35ms
After: ~30ms

## Tasks

- [x] add and run performance test to get initial loading time for compiled code (run 5x to get avg); record the value
- [x] unify zod schemas into large schemas that can be lazily loaded. derive types from there
- [x] change zod schemas in the provider to be lazy loaded (all models, tools, etc) - search for `zod/v4` to identify files
- [x] rename `X-api-types` file to `X-api` and move response schemas there
- [x] check satisfies with z.infer has been updated to InferValidator
- [x] rerun performance test to get updated number (run 5x to get avg); record the value
- [x] add changeset

## Related Issues

Follow-up from #9275

title: feat(provider/anthropic): add prompt caching validation
body:
Fix Anthropic's prompt caching feature:

- Add cache_control support to all content types and tool definitions
- Implement CacheControlValidator to enforce 4 breakpoint limit
- Add TTL support (5m/1h) to cache control type
- Prevent caching on thinking blocks and nested tool result content
- Centralize warning collection to avoid duplicates
- Add cache_control to provider tool types (set to undefined in SDK)

Changes include proper type definitions with cache_control?: never for disallowed locations, validation tests, and backward compatibility.

## Background

Anthropic's prompt caching API has specific constraints that must be followed:
- Maximum of 4 cache breakpoints per request
- `cache_control` can only be used on specific content types (not on nested content blocks within tool results)
- `cache_control` cannot be set on thinking blocks or redacted thinking blocks

Without proper validation, developers can inadvertently create invalid configurations that either fail at runtime or are silently ignored by the API.

## Summary

This PR adds comprehensive validation for Anthropic's prompt caching feature to catch configuration errors early and provide clear guidance to developers.

**Key changes:**

1. **CacheControlValidator class** (`get-cache-control.ts`)
   - Tracks and enforces the 4 cache breakpoint limit per request
   - Validates that `cache_control` is only used in supported contexts
   - Generates helpful warnings when invalid configurations are detected

2. **Updated type definitions** (`anthropic-messages-api.ts`)
   - Added `AnthropicNestedTextContent`, `AnthropicNestedImageContent`, and `AnthropicNestedDocumentContent` types
   - These nested types explicitly prevent `cache_control` via `cache_control?: never`
   - Updated `AnthropicToolResultContent` to use nested types, preventing cache_control on sub-content blocks (per Anthropic docs)

3. **Integration** (`convert-to-anthropic-messages-prompt.ts`, `anthropic-prepare-tools.ts`)
   - Integrated validator into message and tool conversion logic
   - Validator tracks cache breakpoints across system messages, user messages, assistant messages, and tools
   - Returns warnings array that can be surfaced to developers

4. **Test coverage**
   - Added tests for cache breakpoint limit enforcement
   - Tests for warning generation on invalid configurations
   - Tests for proper handling of nested content blocks

## Manual Verification

1. Created test cases with more than 4 cache breakpoints - validator correctly limits to 4 and generates warnings
2. Attempted to set `cache_control` on nested content in tool results - correctly prevented by TypeScript types
3. Verified that valid cache_control configurations continue to work as expected
4. Checked that warnings are properly propagated through the API

## Checklist

- [x] Tests have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Documentation has been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] A _patch_ changeset for relevant packages has been added (for bug fixes / features - run `pnpm changeset` in the project root)
- [x] Formatting issues have been fixed (run `pnpm prettier-fix` in the project root)
- [x] I have reviewed this pull request (self-review)

## Future Work

- Consider adding documentation examples showing proper cache_control usage patterns

## Related Issues

Related to Anthropic prompt caching API requirements and constraints.

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

## Background

Bright Data provides enterprise-grade web scraping and data collection capabilities that enable AI agents to access public web data at scale without getting blocked by anti-bot systems. This integration adds Bright Data tools to the toolkit documentation, allowing developers to build AI agents that can search, extract, and navigate the web reliably.

## Summary

This PR adds Bright Data integration to the AI SDK toolkit documentation. The integration provides:

- **Web Scraping Tool**: Scrape any website and return content in clean markdown or HTML format, bypassing anti-bot protection and CAPTCHAs
- **Search Tool**: Search the web using Google, Bing, or Yandex with anti-bot bypass
- **Amazon Product Tool**: Get detailed Amazon product information, including price, ratings, reviews, and specifications
- **LinkedIn Profile Tool**: Fetch LinkedIn profile data with work experience, education, and skills

4. **LinkedIn Profiles**: Collected profile data from LinkedIn URLs with complete work history

- Error cases (invalid URLs, network errors, API failures)

title: docs(amazon-bedrock): add API key authentication documentation
body:
## Background

  The Amazon Bedrock provider recently added support for API key authentication via the `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` environment variable and `apiKey` parameter.
  However, the documentation was missing this information, and the package README contained incorrect references to a non-existent `withSettings()` method.

  ## Summary

  - Added API key authentication documentation as the recommended method for Amazon Bedrock
  - Fixed incorrect `bedrock.withSettings()` references to use `createAmazonBedrock()` instead
  - Added `apiKey` parameter to provider settings documentation
  - Documented authentication precedence: API key → environment variable → SigV4

title: fix(ai): handle backpressure in `writeToServerResponse`
body:
## Background

`writeToServerResponse` reads from the `ReadableStream` in a tight loop and calls `response.write(value)` without checking the return value or waiting for the `'drain'` event. Under slow clients, Node buffers the excess data in memory, which can grow indefinitely.

## Summary

Add check for backpressure to `writeToServerResponse`

## Manual Verification

Verified fix with demo:

[stream-backpressure-dos-ai-5.0.34.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22892580/stream-backpressure-dos-ai-5.0.34.zip)

title: fix(provider/anthropic): add url-based PDF support in tool results
body:
## Background

This PR adds support for url-based PDFs in tool results. This is a pretty common way to fetch and insert PDF without blowing up the context window. Anthropic's API handles this [out of the box](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/pdf-support). Just needed to update the types on the tool result handling.

## Summary

This PR adds support for url-based PDF support without changing the language model spec. It checks if the data passed back from the tool is a valid url and if so converts the tool result block into the correct PDF content block.

This is a new PR instead of this previous PR with spec changes: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/9041

It also built off of work from this PR that supports base64 PDFs: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/9148

## Manual Verification

Added an example file that shows that the changes work.

title: feat: tool execution approval for dynamic tools
body:
## Background

Tool execution approvals were introduced for static tools in #8541 . Dynamic tools need to support tool execution approvals as well, in particular in preparation for provider-executed MCP servers.

## Summary

Add tool execution approval support for dynamic tools.

## Manual Verification

- [x] run `examples/ai-core/src/generate-text/openai-tool-approval-dynamic-tool.ts`
   - [x] with positive approval responses and follow up message
   - [x] with negative approval responses and follow up message
- [x] run `examples/ai-core/src/stream-text/openai-tool-approval-dynamic-tool.ts`
   - [x] with positive approval responses and follow up message
   - [x] with negative approval responses and follow up message
- [x] run UI test `next-openai` http://localhost:3000/test-tool-approval-dynamic
   - [x] approved with follow up message
   - [x] denied with follow up message
   - [x] multiple approvals in one message

## Tasks

- [x] add generateText example
- [x] change dynamic tool signatures
- [x] fix invalid prompt error for generate with negative response and follow up message
- [x] add streamText example
- [x] add UI example
- [x] add approval UI message states to dynamic tool parts
- [x] process ui stream: parse dynamic tool approvals
- [x] chat submission
- [x] ui message validation
- [x] convert to model messages
- [x] changeset

## Related Issues

Builds on #8541

title: fix(ui): do not submit automatically when server return with error
body:
## Background

When `sendAutomaticallyWhen` is configured and the server responds with an error, an infinite client-server loop is triggered (see #9384 ).

## Summary

Only resubmit automatically when there is no error.

## Manual Verification

Fix manually verified as part of #9518

## Related Issues

Fixes #9384

title: feat(provider/anthropic): mcp connector support
body:
## Background

Anthropic supports [MCP connectors](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/mcp-connector) for calling MCP servers during the LLM call execution.

## Summary

Add Anthropic MCP connector support.

## Manual Verification

- [x] run `examples/ai-core/src/generate-text/anthropic-mcp.ts`
- [x] run `examples/ai-core/src/stream-text/anthropic-mcp.ts`
- [x] run http://localhost:3000/chat-anthropic-mcp with follow up message

## Tasks

- [x] spec change content (support dynamic tool calls and outputs)
- [x] add anthropic provider options for mcp server configuration
- [x] add generateText example
- [x] process anthropic provider options for mcp server configuration (with unit test)
- [x] process anthropic mcp server tool call and send it back as a dynamic tool call (generate)
- [x] process anthropic mcp server tool result and send it back as a dynamic tool result (generate)
- [x] fix generateText for dynamic provider executed tools
- [x] stream example
- [x] stream unit test
- [x] stream implementation
- [x] streamtext fixes
- [x] ui test
- [x] dynamic flag lost in ui transfer
- [x] fix ui message stream
- [x] add provider-executed flag to dynamic tool ui message parts
- [x] anthropic type: "mcp" info
- [x] convertToModelMessages provider executed flag
- [x] convert to anthropic prompt
- [x] rm console log
- [x] docs
- [x] changeset

## Future Work

* support citations from mcp tools
* figure out collision handling when dynamic tools have the same name as a static tool
* support ui message validation with tools when there are provider executed dynamic tools

## Related Issues

Part of #8887
Fixes #9545

# Improve Auth Error Messages for AI Gateway

## Background

Authentication error messages in the AI Gateway were verbose and lacked clear guidance on how to resolve authentication issues. This change improves the user experience by providing more concise error messages with direct links and commands to help users resolve authentication problems.

## Summary

This PR enhances authentication error messages in the AI Gateway by:

- Adding direct links to create API keys
- Including specific commands like `npx vercel link` and `vc env pull` to guide users
- Simplifying error messages with clearer instructions for both API key and OIDC token authentication
- Organizing the "no authentication" error message into clear numbered options
- Removing unnecessary verbose explanations while keeping essential information

## Manual Verification

Verified that the updated error messages appear correctly when authentication fails, and that the links and commands provided are accurate.

title: feat(provider/anthropic): implement support for Claude Agent Skills
body:
## Background

Anthropic recently announced [Agent Skills](https://www.anthropic.com/news/agent-skills), which enable Claude to perform specialized tasks like document processing (PPTX, DOCX, PDF, XLSX) and data analysis. Skills run in a sandboxed container and require code execution to be enabled.

## Summary

Added support for Claude Agent Skills to the Anthropic provider:

- Added `skills` and `betas` arrays to `providerOptions.anthropic` with support for both built-in Anthropic skills and custom skills
- Modified request building to include `container.skills` array and user-specified beta headers
- Added 6 test cases covering request payload, beta headers, multiple skills, and version defaults
- Documented feature in `05-anthropic.mdx` with usage examples

Skills are configured per-request via `providerOptions`, following the existing MCP pattern. Users explicitly need to specify beta headers.

## Manual Verification

- [x] run `examples/ai-core/src/generate-text/anthropic-skills.ts`
- [x] run UI example http://localhost:3000/chat-anthropic-code-execution

## Checklist

- [x] Tests have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Documentation has been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] A _patch_ changeset for relevant packages has been added (for bug fixes / features - run `pnpm changeset` in the project root)
- [x] Formatting issues have been fixed (run `pnpm prettier-fix` in the project root)
- [x] I have reviewed this pull request (self-review)

## Tasks

- [x] automatic headers
- [x] check for code execution tool and warn
- [x] add ui example
- [x] test ui example with multi-message chat
- [x] update docs

## Future Work

- Support for Skills API endpoints (create, list, retrieve, delete custom skills)
- Support for custom agent skills executed / orchestrated through AI SDK and not necessarily using Anthropic but being LLM provider agnostic

## Related Issues

Resolves https://github.com/vercel/ai/issues/9595

body:
<!--
Welcome to contributing to AI SDK! We're excited to see your changes.

We suggest you read the following contributing guide we've created before submitting:

https://github.com/vercel/ai/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

## Background

Google released on the 17th of October the Google Maps Search Grounding tool
- [Blog Post](https://blog.google/technology/developers/grounding-google-maps-gemini-api/)
- [Documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/maps-grounding#whats_next)

## Summary

Adding new Google Maps search grounding tool #9645 

<!-- What did you change? -->

## Manual Verification

<!--
For features & bugfixes.
Please explain how you *manually* verified that the change works end-to-end as expected (excluding automated tests).
Remove the section if it's not needed (e.g. for docs).
-->

1. Installed the package locally on a new local folder
2. Added my `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY`
3. Made a tool call using a simple snippet
	```ts
	import { google } from "@ai-sdk/google";
	import { googleTools } from "@ai-sdk/google/internal";
	import { generateText, stepCountIs, streamText } from "../ai/packages/ai";
	
	const result = await generateText({
	```
